officialSummary: Today, the Reserve Bank released the October 2026 issue of its monthly Bulletin. The Bulletin includes two speeches, four articles and current statistics. The four articles are: I. State of the Economy ; II. Transmission to Lending Rates of SCBs: Price versus Composition Effects in WALR ; III. Performance of the NBFC Sector: Review for 2025 ; and IV. Nowcasting State-Level Economic Activity in India with Night-Time Light and Google Trends . I. State of the Economy Renewed geopolitical frictions in West Asia and supply chain disruptions have amplified inflationary pressures, prompting major central banks to raise policy rates. Elevated sovereign bond yields in advanced economies (AEs) have also brought into focus concerns about fiscal sustainability and its implications for financial stability. The Indian economy continued to demonstrate strength as evidenced by high-frequency indicators across both industry and services. The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation edged up in September driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel, and core components. Double-digit growth in merchandise exports during the first six months of 2026-27 helped in narrowing the trade deficit. FDI, ECB and remittance flows strengthened in August. Strong inflows under the FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves. II. Transmission to Lending Rates of SCBs: Price versus Composition Effects in WALR By Yuvraj Kashyap, Kamal Gupta and Arvind Jha This article analyses the transmission of monetary policy to the fresh lending rates of scheduled commercial banks by decomposing variations in the weighted average lending rate (WALR) into interest rate effects and compositional effects. Using an index-number based framework on bank and sector level lending rates and loan weights, the study examines the extent to which changes in the aggregate WALR reflect changes in lending rates and shifts in credit composition. Highlights: In response to a cumulative reduction of 125 basis points (bps) in the p
title: RBI Bulletin – October 2026

officialSummary: The Reserve Bank of India had issued Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions) Directions, 2025 on November 28, 2025 . 2. Chapter IV of these Directions prescribed the Minimum Capital Requirements for Operational Risk, wherein it was specified that the effective date of implementation and indicative mapping of the components of the Business Indicator (BI) to the schedules and line items of the financial statements shall be provided in due course. Subsequently, Governor in his Statement dated October 01, 2025 , announced that the revised Basel III capital adequacy framework for Commercial Banks (excluding Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Payment Banks (PBs), Regional Rural Banks(RRBs)) would come into effect from April 01, 2027. Further, post issuance of these Directions, certain additional clarifications have been issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. 3. In view of the above developments, the Reserve Bank has today released the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 , specifying the implementation date for the new Standardised Approach (‘Basel III Standardised Approach’ or ‘Basel III SA’) for minimum operational risk regulatory capital requirements, providing an indicative mapping of BI components, and incorporating additional clarifications. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1380
title: RBI issues Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 on Minimum Capital Requirements for Operational Risk
